brief.title: Midterm brief: Saturday, October 24
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Saturday, October 24

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats, and Cook now has 220 D / 198 R with 17 tossups, up from 214 / 200 / 21 ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 10 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 91.5% for the House and 67.5% for the Senate ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 24.

## What moved
- **Forecaster updates (Oct 23):** 27 rating changes, 25 toward Democrats ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). Cook made 19, all toward Democrats.
- **House consensus:** NC-11 moved from Tossup to Lean D; KY-06 from Tilt R to Tossup; CO-04 from Likely R to Lean R (now tracked); TX-28 from Lean D to Likely D (no longer tracked).
- **Ohio Senate special:** The Economist moved it back from Tossup to Lean D; consensus stays Tossup ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)).
- **Polls:** Nebraska Senate's average moved from R+1.0 to R+3.0 across 2 polls; TX-34 moved from D+3.0 to D+7.0 on one poll.

## Races to watch today
- **Alaska Senate (Tossup):** The NYT reports Trump officials asked a court to block certification of the results if Sullivan loses ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/23/us/politics/justice-dept-alaska-senate-race-sullivan.html)). Average: D+0.8.
- **Maine Senate (Tossup):** The administration moved to lift tariffs on some Canadian goods ahead of Collins's tight race ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/23/business/trump-susan-collins-canada-tariffs.html)). Average: D+2.2.
- **Ohio Senate special (Tossup):** NPR reports rural voters may decide the race and possibly Senate control ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/23/nx-s1-6012809/ohio-senate-governor-election-rural-voters)). Average: D+3.5.
- **Michigan Senate (Lean D):** El-Sayed needs Black voters, and tensions with Arab Americans complicate that ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/24/us/politics/el-sayed-black-voters-arab-tensions.html)). Average: D+2.6.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 22, 1,269,919 ballots were cast, 137% of the 2022 total at the same point (927,708) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-23%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 23 the total reached 1,453,517 at D 41.4% / R 24.0% / other 34.6% ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Large states (Oct 23):** Florida has 2,309,424 ballots (998,235 in person) at D 40.0% / R 39.5%, against registration of D 30.1% / R 41.5%; California 2,762,552 at D 50.1% / R 28.9%; Pennsylvania 771,806 at D 66.6% / R 24.3% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from secretary of state data).
- **Senate battlegrounds (Oct 23):** Arizona 759,605 at D 38.7% / R 38.5% (via a private compiler); Maine 178,680 at D 50.2% / R 21.3%; Iowa 207,774 at D 50.9% / R 32.0%; Nebraska 136,433 at D 41.4% / R 42.0% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/)).

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** No new left-leaning episode today; Pod Save America's latest is titled "Fake Polls, Real Wave?" ([Pod Save America](https://audioboom.com/posts/8968285)).
- **Center-left:** The NYT explains why Democrats could find it hard to win the Senate despite strong polls ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/24/us/politics/democrats-expectations-blue-wave.html)).
- **Center-right:** The WSJ reports Republican operatives worry that a run of damaging stories is feeding voter concerns about corruption ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/midterm-election-poll-government-graft-corruption-6493ed51?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)).
- **Right:** National Review criticizes El-Sayed's comparison of himself to JFK ([National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/10/the-problem-with-abdul-el-sayeds-jfk-analogy/)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- The generic ballot averages D+7.2 across 4 polls, down from D+8.0 after an older September YouGov poll left the window; Pew has D+8, ending Oct 4 ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms)).
- Obama returns to the campaign trail, setting up dueling appearances with Trump ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/24/us/politics/obama-trump-midterms-campaign.html)).

## Coverage note
All 24 sources reported, and early vote covered 27 states. Kalshi had no priced markets. Candidate parties remain unresolved for seven House races (FL-22, NV-02, NY-21, NC-11, SC-01, TX-23, TX-35).
